candidate_definitions.name: formal product-notation agreement
candidate_definitions.from: not exists q in I+ and t0 in [0,T) with gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M.
candidate_definitions.to: not exists (q,t0) in I+ x [0,T) with gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M.
candidate_definitions.rationale: the ordered prefix declares ONE not_exists quantifier over the pair (q,t0); the product-domain spelling is the standard notation for that joint quantifier and is logically equivalent to the current independent-quantifier spelling because the domains I+ and [0,T) are independent. The literal binder '(q,t0)' then occurs in the formal sentence and R03's literal-substring test passes without any detector change.
candidate_definitions.expected: structural pass; frozen semantic stage accept with failed_rules []; full pipeline PASS rc 0; union 31/31
candidate_definitions.semantics_risk: surface notation only; the formal sentence's truth conditions are unchanged (both spellings denote: there do not exist q in I+, t0 in [0,T) with the visibility property).
